about: Sanity principles the EmpirePursuit ladder kernel must obey at the shipped gates. The EmpirePursuitFuzz ladder family is a DIFFERENTIAL check: every decision of the kernel is compared with a written spec model, so most laws read 'agrees with the spec', and the direct invariants back them. Each family names a planted kernel defect from src/RimMandrake/Utils/mutate_empirepursuit_fuzz.py that must turn the fuzz red through one of its laws.

laws.sentence: The fire gate (shut inside the storyteller spacing, while terminal, or while a contact is live) equals the written spec's gate on every step.
Whether the ladder fires equals the written spec's decision.
A ladder rung never fires within the storyteller spacing of the last storyteller raid.
Each map's ladder state (next rung, terminal, timers) equals the written spec's after every step.
The next rung the kernel picks equals the written spec's pick, from the same state.
A fired rung is never below the ladder's next rung (the ladder never steps back by firing).
A contact's outcome and its visibility change equal the written spec's for its kind.
A postponed or revived rung is always scheduled after the current tick, never at or before it.

check.text: would be scheduled at or before this tick

laws.sentence: A scheduled raid is at least one hour (2,500 ticks) after the moment it is scheduled.

check.text: is under an hour from now

laws.sentence: A raid warning is at least an hour from now and never after its raid.
With no warning hours set, the warning is the raid itself.

check.text: no warning hours but warn != raid

laws.sentence: A timer fires on the first hourly tick at or after it, and a tick already on the hour stays where it is.

check.text: TimerIntervalTick is not the next hour boundary

laws.sentence: Walking the hourly ticks, a scheduled rung fires exactly once, on its own hour tick.
A warning set before its raid's hour fires exactly once, on its own hour tick, before the raid.

check.text: warning hits {warnHits} at {firstWarn}, want one at {warnTick} before {raidTick}

laws.sentence: A warning that falls on its raid's hour tick never fires on its own.

check.text: warning fired on the raid tick

laws.sentence: No warning and no rung fire while a contact is live or the ladder is terminal.

check.text: a live contact must block warn/fire

laws.sentence: A postponed rung fires on an hour tick later than the one that postponed it.

check.text: postponed rung would fire on or before the tick that postponed it

laws.sentence: With every gate open, endless waves fire exactly once per interval.

check.text: endless waves fired {hits} times in 6 intervals

laws.sentence: A raid is repelled exactly when at least 60% of its raiders are dead or downed (or it had none).
A clamped rung is between 1 and 6 and never under the floor (where the floor is on the ladder).
After a success the next rung is one higher than the one fired, at least the floor and at most 6.
After a failure the next rung is the one fired, raised to the floor if under it, at most 6.
More time away never raises a remembered rung.

check.text: more time away raised the rung

laws.sentence: The permanent floor never goes down.
A remembered higher rung for a tile is where the ladder starts again.

check.text: a remembered higher rung was ignored

plant.name: probe timeout without the extra day
